title: State the page subject in its opening passage
statement: The first substantive paragraph of a page says what the page is about in plain terms, so a system extracting one passage has a self-contained passage to extract rather than an introduction that only makes sense after the rest.
rationale: A passage lifted out of context has to stand alone, and an opening built from scene-setting or a marketing preamble carries no statement of the subject for anything to extract.
implementation: Put the direct answer or definition first and the context after it, keeping the opening readable as prose rather than compressing it into a summary box aimed at machines.

verification.method: Extract the first paragraph of each content route and check that it names the subject without depending on later text.

caution: The cited documentation establishes that one search surface extracts a passage programmatically. It does not describe how assistant retrieval selects text, and no citation, inclusion, or ranking outcome is claimed here. This record is tier B because the extraction mechanism is documented while its effect on assistant answers is not.

title: Attribute statistics and factual claims to their source
statement: A figure, date, or claim of fact carries a reference to where it came from, and that reference points at the party that produced the figure rather than at another page repeating it.
rationale: An unattributed figure cannot be checked by a reader or a machine, and a citation chain that ends at another summary leaves nobody able to reach the measurement itself.
implementation: Link the figure to the primary publication and record when it was checked, replacing links that point at intermediary coverage. Where the original cannot be located, state the limitation instead of citing the summary as though it were the source.

verification.method: Collect numeric and factual assertions from each content route and report those with no outbound reference or with a reference that resolves to another summary of the same figure.

caution: The cited guidance asks whether content demonstrates original reporting and verifiable sourcing, which supports the practice without making it a documented requirement, so this record is tier B. It is justified as content integrity and not as a discoverability mechanism.

title: Do not restructure published prose to suit a retrieval hypothesis
statement: Existing editorial text is not converted into lists, tables, question headings, or summary blocks on the theory that a retrieval system prefers that shape, and any such change is proposed to the author rather than applied.
rationale: The claim that a particular text shape is preferred by assistant retrieval is untested, and acting on it rewrites work whose author chose its form for reasons the untested claim does not weigh.
implementation: Report the observation and leave the text alone. Where a structural change is genuinely warranted by the content, put the case to whoever owns the page and let them decide.

verification.method: Confirm no editorial body text was reshaped by the run, comparing the prose before and after and listing any structural proposal as a recommendation rather than an applied change.

caution: This is a restraint on the agent rather than a property of the site, which is why it carries no external citation. It exists because the retrieval preferences it guards against are widely asserted and nowhere documented.

title: Give each section a stable fragment identifier
statement: Every heading that introduces a distinct section carries an identifier that survives edits to the heading text, so a link to that passage keeps resolving after the wording changes.
rationale: An identifier derived from the heading text breaks whenever the heading is reworded, which silently invalidates every link anyone made to that section.
implementation: Assign the identifier once and keep it, rather than regenerating it from the current heading on each build. Where an identifier must change, leave the previous one in place as an additional target.

verification.method: Collect section identifiers per route across two builds and report any that changed while the section itself persisted.

caution: The cited specification defines how a fragment resolves to an element, which is the mechanism this record depends on. No retrieval system documents using fragments to cite a passage, so the benefit claimed here is that existing links keep working, not that a passage becomes more citable.

title: Record AI surface observations as experimental evidence
statement: An answer produced by an assistant when asked about the site is recorded as a dated observation of one response, and is never promoted into a statement about how that assistant selects or ranks sources.
rationale: These systems are non-deterministic and change without notice, so a single observed answer supports a note about what was seen on a date and supports nothing about why.
implementation: Store the prompt, the date, the surface, and the response verbatim, and label the entry as an observation. Do not derive a rule from it, and do not change the site on the strength of one.

verification.method: Inspect recorded assistant observations and confirm each carries a date and a prompt, and that no requirement in this registry cites one as its justification.

caution: No citation is possible for this record because it constrains how this registry treats evidence rather than describing the web. Assistant behaviour is not reproducible between runs, so observations are logged and not generalised.

title: Publish corrections in the page body rather than only a changelog
statement: When a published claim turns out to be wrong, the correction appears in the passage that carried the claim, not solely in a revision note elsewhere on the page or in a separate log.
rationale: A system that retrieved the passage holds the passage, so a correction recorded only in a footer or a separate log leaves the wrong sentence intact in every copy that was taken.
implementation: Amend the sentence itself and mark the amendment inline, keeping the revision note as a record of what changed rather than as the only place the correction exists.

verification.method: For each recorded correction, confirm the amended text is present in the passage it belongs to and not only in a revision note.

caution: This record rests on the fact that a retrieved copy is a copy, which needs no citation. How long any particular system holds a copy, or whether it refetches, is not documented by its operator and is not claimed here.
